prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1061; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a rear-end collision in a parking lot and said they were struck while stopped at a row of parked cars. They described hitting their head on the steering wheel and were advised to seek medical attention promptly.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy. Coverage was in force at the time of the reported loss, and nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Called the claimant to take a recorded statement. Their account of the impact matched what was first reported, including the direction of travel and the position of both vehicles.

Entry 4: Police report obtained. Responding officers confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses were identified in the report or during follow-up calls.

Entry 5: Photos submitted by the claimant show the rear bumper and tailgate damage and some scuffing on the other vehicle. The visible damage is largely consistent with the impact described, and I found no indication of earlier damage to the vehicle in prior claim records.

Entry 6: Medical records received for the concussion diagnosis. The injury type and severity fit the force of a collision of this kind, and there is no record of prior injury to the head or neck area.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course, with early follow-up visits and a gradual reduction in appointments as symptoms improved. The provider notes describe steady recovery over the period.

Entry 8: Spoke with the claimant again. They repeated the same account of the collision and the symptoms they experienced, with no changes to key details from any earlier conversation.

Entry 9: Reviewed the full file. The reported injury and vehicle damage are consistent with the described incident, and the claim is ready for the next stage of evaluation.
